states.claim: rtcp_xr is a typed pointer to the same storage region as the byte-addressed pkt parameter.
rb_hdr initially points to the buf subobject of the rtcp_xr packet object.
rb_hdr is advanced through the packet storage by report-block lengths during parsing.
rb_rr_time is set to point at the current rb_hdr storage region when the RR_TIME block fits within the packet bounds.
rb_dlrr is set to point at the current rb_hdr storage region when the DLRR block fits within the packet bounds.
rb_stats is set to point at the current rb_hdr storage region when the STATS block fits within the packet bounds.
rb_voip_mtc is set to point at the current rb_hdr storage region when the VOIP_METRICS block fits within the packet bounds.
rb_rr_time, rb_dlrr, rb_stats, and rb_voip_mtc are initialized to NULL before parsing.

values.claim: pkt_len is the 16-bit network-order RTCP length field converted to host order; the packet is accepted only if (pkt_len + 1) <= size/4, so pkt_len+1 32-bit words fit within size bytes.
rb_hdr starts at rtcp_xr->buf and the parse loop continues while (pj_int32_t*)rb_hdr < (pj_int32_t*)pkt + pkt_len, bounding rb_hdr to pkt_len 32-bit words from pkt.
rb_len is the 16-bit network-order length field of the current report block header converted to host order.
rb_hdr is advanced by (rb_len + 1) 32-bit words from its current position, i.e. the block length plus the header word.
rb_rr_time is set to rb_hdr only when rb_hdr + sizeof(*rb_rr_time) <= pkt + size, so the RR_TIME block is fully within the size-byte packet.
rb_dlrr is set to rb_hdr only when rb_hdr + sizeof(*rb_dlrr) <= pkt + size, so the DLRR block is fully within the size-byte packet.
rb_stats is set to rb_hdr only when rb_hdr + sizeof(*rb_stats) <= pkt + size, so the STATS block is fully within the size-byte packet.
rb_voip_mtc is set to rb_hdr only when rb_hdr + sizeof(*rb_voip_mtc) <= pkt + size, so the VOIP_METRICS block is fully within the size-byte packet.
eedelay is computed as now - lrr - dlrr in 64-bit arithmetic, where now, lrr, and dlrr are 32-bit values in 1/65536-second units.
values.evidence:
L96: now = ((ntp.hi & 0xFFFF) << 16) + (ntp.lo >> 16);
L99: eedelay = now - lrr - dlrr;

values.claim: eedelay is converted to microseconds: if eedelay < 4294, eedelay = (eedelay * 1000000) >> 16; otherwise eedelay = ((eedelay * 1000) >> 16) * 1000.
rtt is the low 32 bits of eedelay, and is only used when eedelay <= 30,000,000 microseconds.
If rtt exceeds 3 times sess->stat.rtt.mean and sess->stat.rtt.n != 0, rtt is clamped to (unsigned)sess->stat.rtt.mean*3.
sess->rx_lrr is formed from the low 16 bits of ntp_sec shifted left 16, ORed with the high 16 bits of ntp_frac.
signal_lvl is sign-extended from an 8-bit two's-complement value: if rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl > 127, subtract 256, then cast to pj_int8_t.
values.evidence:
L210: sess->stat.tx.voip_mtc.signal_lvl = (pj_int8_t)
L211: ((rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl > 127)?
L212: ((int)rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl - 256) :
L213: rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl);

values.claim: noise_lvl is sign-extended from an 8-bit two's-complement value: if rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl > 127, subtract 256, then cast to pj_int8_t.
values.evidence:
L214: sess->stat.tx.voip_mtc.noise_lvl  = (pj_int8_t)
L215: ((rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl > 127)?
L216: ((int)rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl - 256) :
L217: rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl);
